The pill has only the thumb's position and the track's color to say which way it's set. The sky-400 track against a white card is 2.2:1, and the slate-200 off track is 1.2:1, both short of the 3:1 WCAG asks of a control's boundary. The thumb's shadow is what lifts it off the track, since white on slate-200 is 1.2:1 on its own. On the dark surface the sky-400 track clears 3:1 and the slate-800 off track does not, at 1.4:1 against slate-700. There the white thumb carries the state instead, at 14.7:1 against its track. The inactive label runs at about 2:1 against the track and the disabled label at 2.5:1. Both are deliberately quiet. The inactive label is a preview of the other state rather than the current one, and disabled controls are exempt from the contrast rules.

A modal is a panel over the page, for a task that has to be finished or abandoned before anything else happens. It renders at the end of rather than where you wrote it, so no ancestor's overflow or stacking context can clip it. Four slots make the panel, top to bottom. header is the title, rendered as an h2. subheader sits under it in the same white bar. The default slot is the body, tinted to slate-50, and the body is the part that scrolls. footer is the action bar, white again and pinned under the body. v-model is the boolean that opens and closes it. The modal also emits close when it closes itself, for the cases where the open state isn't the only thing that has to be reset.

heading: Head and footer
text: Every region pads its content by 24px and is divided from the next by a slate-100 line. The head and the footer are white, the body is slate-50, so the chrome reads as chrome and the content reads as content. The body is a glass surface and it says so to everything inside it. An Input or a Select in there picks up the right boundary without being told. The head and the footer are default, so a Button in the action bar comes out slate-100. The action bar is always there. A modal ends in its actions, so the bar is part of the shape rather than a slot that comes and goes. The head is the part that can go. Drop header and subheader for a modal whose body speaks for itself, and the body runs to the top edge with no empty bar above it. The close button floats over the panel rather than sitting in the head, so it survives the head going away. Whichever region is at the top holds its end corner clear of it. With a head that's 64px of end padding on the title. With no head it's 56px of top padding on the body, since indenting the body's whole end edge would pull every row in with it. A modal with no header needs an aria-label, since there's no title for the dialog to be named by.

heading: The action bar
text: The footer is a row. Below sm it stacks, reversed, so the last button written is the one on top and closest to the thumb. The primary action fills the bar. Give it block and write it last. A secondary button beside it keeps its own width and the primary takes what's left.

heading: Size
text: The size prop sets the panel's maximum width on screens above sm. The sizes are sm, md (the default), lg, xl, and full. | Size | Max width | | ------ | --------------- | | sm | 28rem | | md | 36rem | | lg | 48rem | | xl | 64rem | | full | the full window | Below sm the size is ignored. The panel is a sheet on the bottom edge at every size, full width, square across the bottom and rounded across the top. It stops 4rem short of the top of the window, so the page behind it stays visible.

heading: Stacking
text: A modal can open another one. Mark the one underneath stacked while the second is open, and it scales back, fades, and blurs behind it. A stacked modal ignores Escape and clicks outside, so the only way out is through the modal on top. Pass :backdrop="false" on the second one. The first modal's backdrop is already there, and a second would double the dimming.

heading: Closing
text: dismissible is on by default. Turn it off and the close button goes, along with the padding that was holding room for it. Escape does nothing and a click outside does nothing. The only way out is a control you put in the modal. Reach for it when leaving halfway through would put something in a broken state. A modal that is merely important still closes.

heading: Backdrop
text: backdrop is on by default and paints slate-300 at 80% over the page. Turn it off for a modal that sits on top of another one, or where the page behind has to stay readable. The page still locks either way. Clicking outside still closes it.

heading: Interaction
text: Opening fades the backdrop in over 200ms and brings the panel up over 300ms, from 4rem below on desktop and from off the bottom edge on mobile. Closing runs at 200ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion the panel only fades. The page behind stops scrolling while a modal is open, and the width the scrollbar leaves behind is added back as padding so nothing shifts. Nested modals count, so the lock lifts when the last one closes. Opening focuses the first input, select, or textarea in the body. With no field to focus, the panel takes focus itself. Closing puts focus back on whatever had it before. Tab and Shift + Tab cycle inside the panel and can't reach the page behind it. Esc closes it, and only the topmost modal answers, so one press closes one modal. Clicking the backdrop closes it, but only when the press started there, so dragging a selection out of the panel doesn't.

heading: Methods
text: A ref on the modal reaches four methods, for the case where the body is a long form and the modal has to move to a part of it. | Method | What it does | | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | scrollTo(options) | Scrolls the body. Defaults to the top, smoothly. | | scrollToElement(element) | Scrolls the element into the body, 80px down from the top edge. | | focusField(index, scroll) | Focuses the nth input, select, or textarea in the body. | | focusInvalidField(index, scroll)| Focuses the nth element in the body marked aria-invalid="true". | focusField and focusInvalidField scroll to what they focus unless you pass false. Both return false when there's nothing at that index.

heading: Contrast
text: | Element | On | WCAG 2.x | | ------------------- | ------------- | -------- | | slate-700 title | white head | 10.4:1 | | slate-500 body text | slate-50 body | 4.6:1 | | slate-50 body | white head | 1.05:1 | | slate-100 divider | white | 1.1:1 | | white panel | backdrop | 1.4:1 | The title and the body text clear AA. The divider and the panel edge do not, and neither is asked to carry meaning. The step from the white head to the slate-50 body is 1.05:1, which is why the slate-100 line is there as well. The panel is told apart from the page by the backdrop's dimming and the shadow under it, not by the 1.4:1 step in lightness.

An alert is a message that sits in the page, for something the reader needs to know about the screen they are on. It fills the width of its container and stays until it is dismissed or its parent removes it. It has a role of alert, so a screen reader announces it when it appears. An alert sits on the label weight from Color: a 100 fill, a 900 label, a 300 border, and a 500 icon. It is the same treatment a Badge gets, at a size that holds a sentence.

heading: Color
text: The color prop sets the tint. The choices are sky (the default), teal, amber, rose, violet, and slate. The meanings come from Color. Teal is success or completion. Amber is caution. Rose is failing or destructive. Sky is the primary thing on the screen. Violet is an accent with no status attached. Slate has no meaning at all.

heading: Calm
text: calm swaps the tinted fill for slate-100 and the border for slate-200, and keeps the color on the text and icon. The text moves from the 900 to the 950 of the hue, since the 900 loses its tint on a slate fill. The message still reads as its color, with less of it on the page.

heading: Surface
text: On a white or glass card the alert carries its 300 border and no shadow. On the page background, or anything slate-200 or darker, it takes a shadow and the border drops to the 50 of the fill. The shadow does the separating, so the border only has to finish the edge. It works that out from the Card it's inside. The page is the one surface with no component to announce it. That's what sitsOn is for. An element that paints a background of its own can wrap its contents in SurfaceProvider instead.

heading: Dismissing
text: The close button is on by default. Pressing it hides the alert and emits close. Bind v-model to bring the alert back, or to know from outside that it went. Left unbound, the alert tracks its own visibility. dismissible off removes the button. The alert then stays until its parent stops rendering it, for a message the reader has to act on rather than wave away.

heading: Actions
text: The actions slot sits between the message and the close button. It holds a Button or two. Only sm buttons go in an alert. A larger one makes the alert taller than the ones around it, and stacked alerts should read as one height. The button takes the alert's color, so the two read as one thing. The alert announces its fill to the slot the way a Card does, so a slate button on a slate alert steps up to slate-300 instead of vanishing into the fill. On a calm alert the button keeps the color the alert gave up.

heading: Description
text: The description slot puts a body under the message. The message becomes the title, the icon and the buttons line up on it, and the description sits underneath in the 800 of the hue, starting where the title starts. Bold the part of the title that matters yourself. A list in the description gets its bullets back. Both are slots rather than props, so part of the title can be bold, or carry a badge.

heading: Icon
text: The icon is a filled exclamation circle at the 500 of the alert's color. The icon slot replaces it. The slot takes the same color, so an icon dropped in needs no class of its own. The icon is decorative, so it needs aria-hidden. The words carry the meaning.

heading: Interaction
text: An alert responds to nothing except its close button, which is a transparent Button at sm. It shows a fill on hover and answers Enter and Space like any button. There is no auto-dismiss. An alert that goes away on its own is a toast, and this system has none yet.

heading: Contrast
text: Every color clears WCAG AAA and APCA's Lc 75 mark for body text. | Fill | Label | WCAG 2.x | APCA | | ----------- | ----------- | -------- | ------ | | sky-100 | sky-900 | 8.2:1 | Lc 82 | | teal-100 | teal-900 | 8.4:1 | Lc 83 | | amber-100 | amber-900 | 8.2:1 | Lc 83 | | rose-100 | rose-900 | 8.0:1 | Lc 78 | | violet-100 | violet-900 | 9.3:1 | Lc 83 | | slate-100 | slate-900 | 16.3:1 | Lc 98 | The 500 icon lands between 1.9:1 and 3.7:1 on its own tint, the same as a badge's icon, so it reinforces the message and never replaces it. A 100 fill barely separates from the surface, so the 300 border is part of the treatment. Badge has the numbers for both.

Use Tabs when a section of a screen has a few alternative blocks of content and only one shows at a time. Each tab names one block. Picking a tab swaps the block below the track without leaving the page. If picking one would take you to another page, it is a link, and it belongs in the Navbar or in the content. A choice that is only a value, with no block to reveal, is not a tab. Neither is a filter that narrows one list. Reach for Radio for both. Tabs sit directly above the content they switch, the full width of the section, under a heading that names the question they answer. There is always a current tab. The first is picked by default, and the panels are never all hidden. On screen, Tabs is a row of choices in a track, with a white pill behind the one that is picked. Picking another slides the pill over to it and swaps the block below. It is four components. Tabs holds the v-model and the settings the others read. TabList is the track and handles the keyboard. Tab is one choice inside the track, with a value and a label. TabPanel is the block for one value, and shows while that tab is picked. The v-model is the value of the picked tab. A tab and a panel with the same value are linked, and the ids and aria-controls and aria-labelledby between them are written for you. Tabs renders a plain with no layout of its own, so the track and the panels go wherever the section needs them, and classes on it are yours. The track is a , each tab a , and each panel a . Give the track a name. Point aria-labelledby at the heading above it, or pass aria-label where there is no heading.

heading: The To step
text: The audience step of the campaign composer. The heading names the question, the track answers it, and each tab reveals the fields for that answer.

heading: Surface
text: Tabs works out what it is sitting on for itself, by asking the Card or Navbar it's inside. The track is the off track of a Switch, surface for surface. It is slate-300, and steps away from the surface where slate-300 would vanish into it. On white it lightens to slate-200. On sunken it goes to slate-400 at 50%. On dark it goes the other way, to slate-800, so the tabs read as a well in the panel. The pill is white everywhere. The panels have no fill of their own and sit straight on the surface. | Sitting on | Which is | Track | | ------------ | ------------ | ------------- | | default | white | slate-200 | | glass | slate-50 | slate-300 | | sunken | slate-300/30 | slate-400/50 | | dark | slate-700 | slate-800 | | background | slate-200 | slate-300 | The unpicked labels are slate-600, and slate-300 on dark where they sit on the slate-800 track. The picked label is slate-800 on its white pill everywhere. The track has a shallow inset shadow and a 1px bottom border in white, so it reads as pressed into the surface. The border is solid white on default and glass, white at 40% on background, white at 30% on sunken, and white at 10% on dark. The page background is the surface nothing can announce. That's what sitsOn is for. An element that paints a background of its own can wrap its contents in SurfaceProvider instead.

heading: Size
text: The size prop on Tabs sets the height of the track, and the text and padding of each tab. The sizes are sm, md (the default), and lg. Each is the height of the labeled Switch and of a Button at the same size, so the three sit level in a toolbar. At md and lg the tabs sit 4px apart, the same as the padding around them, since the space between things never exceeds the space to the edge. At sm the padding is 2px and the tabs touch. | Size | Track | Text | | ---- | ----- | --------- | | sm | 32px | text-xs | | md | 40px | text-xs | | lg | 48px | text-sm |

heading: Disabled
text: disabled on Tabs flattens the track to slate-200 and the pill to slate-50, drops every label to slate-400, and ignores presses. The pill stays where it was, so a disabled set of tabs still shows which one is picked, and its panel stays up. On dark the track is slate-800 at 50%, the pill slate-500, and the labels slate-500 with the picked one slate-300. disabled on a single Tab greys that one out and skips it. Clicks do nothing and the arrow keys pass over it.

heading: Keeping a panel mounted
text: A panel is in the DOM only while its tab is picked. Switch away and whatever was inside it is gone, along with anything typed into it. Pass keepMounted on a TabPanel to keep it in the DOM while hidden, so its fields hold their state.

heading: Interaction
text: Hovering an unpicked tab fills it with slate-400 at 40%, slate-500 at 30% on sunken, and slate-700 on dark. Pressing it pulls that fill in by 2px on every side and shrinks the label to 96%, the same press as a Button. It is an inset and not a scale, so a tab that has grown wide with the track presses the same as a narrow one. The shrink runs motion-safe, and with reduced motion the fill dims to 70% instead. The picked tab and a disabled tab don't hover or press. Clicking the picked tab does nothing, and the cursor stays an arrow over it. The pill takes 200ms to slide from one tab to the next on an ease-out curve, quick and without a bounce, in line with Look and Feel. The label colors cross over in the same 200ms. Tab lands on the picked tab and nowhere else in the track, and a second Tab lands on the panel it reveals, whatever is inside it. From the track, ← and → move to the next tab and pick it as they go, wrapping at either end, and Home and End jump to the first and last. Disabled tabs are skipped. Until something is picked, every tab is in the tab order. Focus draws a blue outline around the tab, two pixels wide at a two pixel offset, and only for keyboard focus. Clicking a tab doesn't ring it. The panel takes the same outline at a four pixel offset when it has the focus. Until the page has hydrated, the picked tab paints its own white in place of the pill, so server-rendered HTML shows a selection and nothing flashes when the pill takes over.

heading: Contrast
text: | Element | On | WCAG 2.x | APCA | | -------------------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------ | | slate-800 label | white pill | 14.7:1 | Lc 101 | | slate-600 label | slate-200 | 6.1:1 | Lc 72 | | slate-600 label | slate-300 | 5.1:1 | Lc 61 | | slate-600 label | slate-400/50 | 4.2:1 | Lc 50 | | slate-600 label | hovered tab | 4.6:1 | Lc 56 | | slate-300 label | slate-800 | 9.9:1 | Lc 77 | | white pill | slate-200 | 1.2:1 | Lc 13 | | white pill | slate-300 | 1.5:1 | Lc 26 | | white pill | slate-400/50 | 1.8:1 | Lc 38 | | white pill | slate-800 | 14.7:1 | Lc 104 | | slate-200 track | white | 1.2:1 | Lc 11 | | slate-300 track | slate-50 | 1.4:1 | Lc 20 | | slate-400/50 track | sunken | 1.4:1 | Lc 16 | | slate-800 track | dark | 1.4:1 | Lc 0 | | slate-400 label | slate-200 | 2.1:1 | Lc 37 | | slate-400 label | slate-50 pill | 2.5:1 | Lc 48 | Every label clears AA on every surface, and the picked one clears AAA on its pill. The slate-600 label on the sunken track is the closest call at 4.2:1. The pill is what says which tab is picked, and on the light surfaces it doesn't clear on color. White on the slate-200 track is 1.2:1, short of the 3:1 WCAG asks of a control's boundary. The pill's shadow lifts it off the track, and the picked label is two steps darker than the rest, so the state survives without the color. On dark the white pill clears at 14.7:1. The disabled labels run at 2.1:1 and 2.5:1. Disabled controls are exempt from the contrast rules, and they are deliberately quiet.

A menu is a short list of actions behind one control. Press the control and a white panel drops under it holding a row per action. Pick one and the panel goes. Its main job is the overflow menu at the end of a list row, where three or four actions have to fit behind a single button. The component is a wrapper and one sub-component. Menu holds the control in its default slot, positions the panel, and opens and closes it. MenuItem is a row in the panel. This is a menu of actions, not a way to pick a value. A control that sets a field is a Select.

heading: The control
text: Whatever you put in the default slot is the control, and a press anywhere on it toggles the panel. Most of the time that's a Button holding an ellipsis, with an aria-label since the icon says nothing on its own. The menu can't put anything inside your control, so two things are yours to set. The slot hands you open for both. aria-haspopup="true" says the button opens something, and :aria-expanded="open" says whether it's showing. The explicit #default template is what lets the slot be destructured.

heading: Items
text: Every row in the items slot is a MenuItem. Give it an href and it renders an . Leave it off and it renders a , and its @click is where the action goes. Either way a press closes the panel. A row is text-xs, semibold, black on white, with 24px of padding at the sides and 16px above and below. Its content is a flex row with the ends pushed apart, so a label written first and an icon written last land at the two edges. Rows are divided by a slate-200 line, and the panel clips the first and last to its corners. The corners are the control's own, read when the panel opens, so a panel under a sm button is rounded to 8px and one under an md button to 12px. A control with square corners gets 8px. disabled fades a row to half and drops its pointer, so it neither presses nor closes the panel. A disabled row stays in the list so the reader can see the action exists. The panel is a and each MenuItem renders its own , so a screen reader announces how many rows there are. Anything in the slot that isn't a MenuItem needs its own .

heading: Placement
text: The placement prop sets which edge of the control the panel lines up with. The choices are left (the default) and right. A menu at the end of a row wants right, so the panel grows back into the row rather than off the edge of the page. The prop is a preference. A panel that would run off the right edge of the window lines up right whatever you asked for, and one that would run off the left edge lines up left.

heading: In a list row
text: The shape the product uses most. A short outline button ends each row, and the panel lines up with its right edge.

heading: Rendering at the end of body
text: The panel is positioned inside the wrapper, so an ancestor that clips its overflow clips the panel too. A scrolling table is the usual one. teleport renders the panel at the end of instead, at the same spot on screen, where nothing can clip it. Open the two menus below. The first is clipped by its box. The second has teleport and isn't. A teleported panel is placed from where the control is on screen and moves with it as the page scrolls. It's still the menu's child in Vue, so it still closes on a click outside, on Esc, and on a row being pressed.

heading: Long menus
text: The panel grows to fit its rows until 16px short of the window edge, then scrolls. The example below holds seventeen rows. A panel opening near the bottom of the window flips to open upward when there's more room above the control than below it. It flips only then, so a panel that fits nowhere at least takes the larger space.

heading: Disabled
text: disabled fades the whole thing to half and stops the control from opening it. Disable the button inside as well, so it doesn't press and can't be reached with Tab.

heading: Interaction
text: The panel opens on click and closes on a second click of the control, on a click anywhere outside, on Esc, or on a row being pressed. Nothing happens on hover. A pointer crossing a list would open menus by accident, and a touchscreen has no hover at all. It sits 8px under the control, or 8px above it when it has flipped, with a slate-200 border and a large shadow. open is two-way. Bind it with v-model:open to drive the menu from outside, or read it to know when the panel is showing. Every row is a real or , so once the panel is open its rows join the tab order. There are no arrow keys and no role="menu", deliberately. This is a disclosure, a button revealing a short list of controls, and Tab moves through everything. role="menu" would commit it to application-menu semantics and the keyboard contract that comes with them. Closing with Esc hands focus back to the control that opened it, when focus was inside.

heading: Contrast
text: | Element | On | WCAG 2.x | | -------------------- | --------- | -------- | | black label | white | 21:1 | | black label, hover | slate-50 | 20.1:1 | | black label, pressed | slate-100 | 19.2:1 | | disabled label | white | 3.9:1 | | slate-200 divider | white | 1.2:1 | The labels clear AA with room to spare, at rest and in both states. The disabled row runs at 3.9:1, which is under AA for text. Disabled controls are exempt, and the row also loses its pointer, so the fade is never the only cue. The divider is far under, and it isn't asked to carry meaning. The rows are told apart by their padding and the panel is told apart from the page by its border and shadow, not by the line between rows.

A popover opens a small white panel beside a control. The panel holds text or interactive content. Clicking the control opens it on mouse, keyboard, and touch. Popover holds the trigger in its default slot. Bind triggerProps to one focusable Button so its expanded state and panel relationship reach assistive technology. The content slot receives close and isOpen. A plain string can use the content prop instead.

heading: Content
text: The panel has a white surface, 16px padding, 8px corners, and a shadow. Components inside it inherit the white surface even when the trigger sits on a dark card. Its width follows the content up to 320px. Longer content scrolls when it reaches the available height.

heading: Hover
text: hover adds mouse hover without taking away click or touch. This example waits 300ms before opening. Moving onto the panel keeps it open. Clicking the trigger keeps it open after the pointer leaves. openDelay defaults to 0 and applies to hover. closeDelay defaults to 150 and gives the pointer time to cross the gap. Click, keyboard, and dismissal respond immediately. Hover leaves keyboard focus where it was. Base UI distinguishes popovers from tooltips by the trigger's purpose. An info control that opens its own content is a popover. A tooltip supplies a supplementary hint for a control with another purpose. This component uses a dialog role and supports controls inside its content.

heading: Placement
text: placement defaults to bottom. The other sides are top, left, and right. Each side accepts -start or -end alignment. auto, auto-start, and auto-end choose the side with the most space. The panel sits 8px from the control. It flips and shifts to stay within the available space, then follows the trigger on scroll and resize. locked stops side flipping for an explicit placement. arrow adds an arrow that follows the final side. arrowPadding keeps it away from the corners and defaults to 8.

heading: Clipping
text: teleport defaults to true, rendering the panel at the end of the document body. The trigger below sits in a box that clips its contents. Its panel remains visible outside that box. Set :teleport="false" to render beside the trigger in the document. Ancestor overflow can then clip it. zIndex defaults to 50.

heading: Controlled state
text: v-model:open reads and changes the open state. The open and close events report visibility changes. Opening from outside leaves focus where it is.

heading: Disabled
text: disabled prevents opening and closes an open panel. Disable the trigger button as well so it leaves the tab order. An empty content prop also prevents opening when there is no content slot.

heading: Interaction
text: Clicking the trigger moves focus to the first control inside the panel, or to the panel itself when it holds only text. Pressing the trigger again closes it. A click outside, focus moving outside, or Esc also closes it. Closing from inside returns focus to the trigger. Clicking elsewhere keeps focus on the destination. Tab moves through the panel's controls, then continues after the trigger. Shift + Tab from the first control closes the panel and returns to the trigger. The panel does not trap focus. The panel takes its accessible name from the trigger. Set label when the panel needs a different name. An icon-only trigger still needs its own aria-label. disableClickAway keeps outside pointer presses from closing the panel. Focus leaving and Esc still dismiss it. interactive defaults to true. Set it to false to close when the panel is clicked.

heading: Migration
text: This component replaces vx-popover. The default trigger slot, content prop, content slot, placement values, and optional arrow carry over. Replace show with v-model:open and bind the default slot's triggerProps to the trigger. The content slot still exposes close and isOpen. The default hover close delay is now 150ms and the default stacking level is 50. Focus alone does not open the panel. Activate the trigger with Enter or Space instead.

A page is made up of two layout sections. The Navbar runs the full width of the window. The main content area has its width capped. Tailwind's container plus a max width and padding determine the main content width. Screens like Message Hub and the workflow builder are exceptions. They drop the max width, because the user needs maximum space for complex or heavy work. Headings should always sit with their content inside cards. Page titles are the exception. They sit directly on the page background. The space between cards is the same on every layout. It never exceeds the padding between the container and the edge of the window. Every layout below is live. View Full Screen will let you preview the layout at production scale.

heading: Base Layout
text: Most pages use a left-aligned 12-column grid that gets filled with content cards. Examples are dashboards, item lists, and analytics. The grid sits at the main content level in the markup, not on the html body. That way it can be dropped in when a page needs it. This also allows content padding and gaps to be managed separately from the navbar.

heading: Create Pages
text: Create pages use a centered, single column layout for a focused flow experience. These are the only pages that do so. Examples include creating a campaign, a segment, or a contact. The column is a flex stack with its cards centered. Each card is full width up to md, then capped at max-w-2xl. A page description sits on the page background, directly under the heading. The cards usually have a glass surface, because they hold form inputs. That card width is shared with the small cards on sidebar pages, so a form looks the same wherever it appears.

heading: Sidebar Pages
text: Some pages require sidebars. Examples include edit screen, analytics, and settings. The sidebar and the content sit in a flex row from md up. Below that the sidebar stacks above the content. The sidebar has a fixed width of w-48 at md and w-56 at lg. The content column takes the remaining width. Small content cards in this layout match the width of the ones in the create screens for consistency. They use the same w-full md:max-w-2xl and sit at the left of the content column. Some content requires more space. In those instances the cards fill the full width of the content column with w-full. A settings page mixes both widths in one column. The overview card and the table rows run the full content width. The form cards and the button bar keep the small card width.
A form is Input and Select stacked in a column, each one carrying its own label, description, and messages. This page is how they go together. The component pages are what each prop does.

heading: Anatomy
text: A field is up to five parts, top to bottom. | Part | What it holds | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Label | What this field is. Always there, apart from the compact case below. | | Description | What the label can't hold. Only when the field needs it. | | The control | The field itself. | | Counter | A bar and a count, for a field with a length limit. See Char Counter. | | Message | The validation message, or the details line. Rose with a warning mark when the field is in error, slate with an info mark otherwise. | Label and description are props on the control rather than a component you stack above it. A field that renders itself whole is a field nobody can forget to label.

heading: Labels
text: Every field gets a label. It's the one part that tells someone what they're filling in, and it's what a screen reader announces when focus lands. The label is extrabold and slate-800, so a form column scans as a list of questions. It sizes with the control, so the label on a sm field is text-xs like the field's own value.

heading: Descriptions
text: Put a description under the label when there's something the reader needs before they type, and it won't fit in a label. It goes above the control, not below it, since it's information for filling the field in rather than feedback on what was filled in. Anything that only matters after the fact belongs in the message line under the control instead.

heading: Placeholders
text: Avoid placeholder text. A field with grey text in it reads as a field that already has an answer, so people skip it, and the moment they start typing the text is gone. Whatever the placeholder was going to say belongs in the label or the description.

heading: Compact fields
text: A compact field is one in a row that reads as a sentence, where a label above every control would break the line. Automation filters and actions are the case this exists for. There, drop the label and let a placeholder carry the name of the field. This is the exception, not a second style to choose from. A field in a form column takes a label.

heading: Messages
text: One line under the control, with a mark at the start of it. The error is rose-800 with a warning mark. The details line is slate-600 with an info mark, for validation notes and formatting tips. A field can show both, with the error above. Color alone doesn't carry the error, which is why the mark is there. aria-invalid and aria-describedby are set for you when error is passed.

heading: Actions
text: When a form ends in two buttons, the primary goes on the right and fills the width, and the secondary sits on the left at its own width.

A skill is a set of instructions written for an AI agent. It covers one job, like laying out a page or building a form, and tells the agent how to do that job the Voxie way. The docs under /docs explain the system to a person. Skills say the same things as rules an agent can follow.

heading: Why skills exist
text: An agent working in a Voxie codebase has no way to know the conventions on its own. Left alone, it will pick its own colors, its own spacing, and its own component shapes. A skill closes that gap. It hands the agent the rules up front, so the output lands inside the system instead of needing to be pulled back into it.

heading: How skills are used
text: Each skill is a folder in this repo's skills/ directory holding a SKILL.md, the format Claude Code reads natively. Once a skill is installed in a project, Claude Code loads its description on every turn and pulls in the full instructions on its own when a task matches. Nobody has to remember the skill exists or paste anything in. In product-prototypes this is already set up. Clone the repo, run pnpm install, and start Claude Code in that directory. The vui skills are there. To set up another repo, add vui as a git submodule and run the link script from your package.json, so every install refreshes the links: The script symlinks each skill into the repo's .claude/skills/, adds new ones, and removes links for skills that no longer exist. Commit the symlinks, so a fresh checkout has them before anyone runs install. To update, bump the submodule and run pnpm install again. For a tool that reads a URL instead, like Cursor or Copilot, each skill is also a page under /skills/. Give the agent the URL, or paste the page's contents into the prompt, and tell it to follow the instructions before making changes. This is one-shot, so repeat it in each new conversation.

heading: Reviewing the result
text: A skill is a summary. The docs page it is based on is the source of truth. Check the output against those pages, and fix the skill when the two disagree.
A form is a column of fields, each carrying its own label, description, and messages. Source of truth: /docs/patterns/forms, /docs/components/input, /docs/components/select.

heading: Anatomy
text: Top to bottom, a field is up to five parts: Label. Always present, apart from the compact case below. font-extrabold text-slate-800, sized with the control (text-xs on a small field). A form column should scan as a list of questions. Description. Only when the label cannot hold what the reader needs before typing. Sits above the control, never below. The control. Inputs stand out subtly from a glass card, which is why form cards are usually glass. Counter. A bar and a count, only for a field with a length limit. Message. One line under the control with a mark at the start. Error: rose-800 with a warning mark. Details: slate-600 with an info mark. Both can show, error first.

heading: Rules
text: No placeholders. Grey text in a field reads as an answer, so people skip it, and it vanishes on typing. Put the words in the label or description. Compact fields are the one exception. A row that reads as a sentence, like automation filters ("When [field] is [value]"), drops the label and lets a placeholder name the field. A field in a form column always takes a label. Color alone never carries an error. The mark is required. Set aria-invalid and aria-describedby when a field is in error. Feedback goes below, guidance goes above. Anything that matters before typing is a description. Anything that matters after is a message.

heading: Actions
text: When a form ends in two buttons, the primary goes on the right and fills the width, written last. The secondary sits on the left at its own width. The primary is sky only if it is the screen's primary action. Otherwise it stays slate.

heading: Review checklist
text: Every field has a visible label, extrabold, slate-800. No placeholder text outside a compact inline row. Descriptions above the control, messages below with a mark. The form card is glass and capped at max-w-2xl. Two-button row: primary right and full width, secondary left.

Voxie is a dense product that should feel light and approachable. Soft shapes, quiet slate surfaces, a small set of accents used deliberately, and content that lifts off a grey page. Tailwind classes are the vocabulary. Use real color names (bg-slate-200, text-sky-700), never semantic aliases like primary or danger. The full reasoning and every measured value lives in the docs. This file is the working summary. When something here leaves room for doubt, the docs win: /docs/foundations/color, /docs/foundations/typography, /docs/foundations/icons, /docs/components/button, /docs/components/card.

heading: Surfaces
text: Almost everything is slate. The page is bg-slate-200. Panels rise above it or sink below it. | Surface | Classes | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | default | bg-white shadow-sm rounded-2xl | The workhorse card: callouts, stats, dashboard panels, list rows | | glass | bg-slate-50 border border-white shadow-sm rounded-2xl | Panels holding inputs: settings, forms, sidebars | | glass raised | bg-white/80 border border-white shadow-2xl backdrop-blur-lg rounded-2xl | Floating sticky bars and in-page nav, only on the page background | | sunken | bg-slate-300/30 shadow-inner border-b border-b-white rounded-2xl | Sidebars and collapsible containers | | dark | bg-slate-700 | Only the app navigation bar | Card padding is p-6 by default, p-4 for dense rows and sidebars, p-8 for focused flows and modals, none when the card wraps a table or image. Cards never have hover styles. If a card leads somewhere, put a button in it.

heading: Neutrals step one rung
text: A neutral element (a slate button, a chip, a row highlight) sits one rung away from what is behind it. Hover moves one more rung in the same direction. | Behind it | Neutral | Hover | | --- | --- | --- | | white | slate-100 | slate-200 | | slate-50 | slate-200 | slate-300 | | slate-200 (page) | slate-300 | slate-400 | | slate-300/30 | slate-300 | slate-400 | | slate-700 | slate-600 | slate-500 | That one-rung step is 1.1:1 to 1.4:1 contrast, which is deliberate and calm. It also means the fill alone never tells someone a control is there. The label carries it. Never signal state with a one-rung neutral shift.

heading: Accent colors
text: The palette is sky, teal, amber, rose, violet. Each has a meaning: sky: the primary action. One per screen, ideally. Also a positive trend on a chart. Voxie uses sky, never green, for "good". teal: success or completion. amber: caution, nothing broken. Sparingly, attention outside warning semantics (the Quick Blast button). rose: destructive or failing. Delete, disconnect, error. violet: accent with no status. Sparingly. Current uses: AI, segments, badge callouts. An accent appears at exactly one of two weights: Controls (anything pressable) rest at 300 with a black label. Hover is 400. bg-sky-300 hover:bg-sky-400 text-black. Accents hold this value on every surface, including the dark bar. Labels (read only: badges, alerts) use the tint. 100 fill, 900 text, 300 border, 500 icon. bg-sky-100 text-sky-900 border border-sky-300. Be reserved. If everything has a color, nothing is important. A word is the default, and color, bold, an icon, or a chart is justified only when the word alone does not carry the meaning.

heading: Text
text: Four text colors on a surface, and only four: | Color | Use | | --- | --- | | slate-700 | Body copy. The default. Never black or slate-950 for body. | | slate-800 | Headings, strong, code, anything cutting through a paragraph | | slate-500 | Supporting copy that steps back, never a disabled state. Only at large sizes on the page background or sunken surface. | | sky-700 | Links. sky-600 fails AA on white, so links stay at 700. | Labels on a fill are black on any accent 300 and on white through slate-300, white on slate-600 and slate-700, and the 900 of the hue on a 100 tint. White on a light fill is never right.

heading: Typography
text: Inter, self-hosted variable. The default size is text-sm, since this is working UI, not reading material. | Size | Use | | --- | --- | | text-5xl leading-none | Stat callouts | | text-2xl xl:text-3xl | Page headings on the page background | | text-xl | Card headings at the top of the range, h2, h1 inside a card | | text-lg / text-base | Card headings and sub content | | text-sm | Body copy, sidebar headings | | text-xs | Dense UI | | text-2xs (10px, custom) | Small badges, calendar day labels. Never a heading. | Headings are font-extrabold, and font-semibold when nested or sitting back. Body is normal weight. Weight does the work of size, so headings stay close in size. Never all caps. Leading is leading-relaxed for multi-line body, leading-snug for most headings, leading-tight for compact controls, leading-none for the largest. Numbers are tabular (tabular-nums on body). In dense lists, headings truncate to one line and body clamps to two. Elsewhere let text wrap, with text-balance on headings.

heading: Buttons
text: font-semibold, whitespace-nowrap, label black on any light fill. Sizes: | Size | Classes | | --- | --- | | xs | h-6 px-2 text-xs rounded-lg | | sm | h-8 px-3 text-xs rounded-lg | | md (default) | h-10 px-4 text-xs rounded-xl | | lg | h-12 px-5 text-sm rounded-xl | | xl | h-16 px-8 text-sm rounded-2xl | Slate is the default fill and follows the one-rung table above. Reach for a color only when the button earns it. Outline drops the fill and keeps the border. White has no border and needs a colored or dark surface, or a shadow. Transparent has no fill until hover. Disabled is opacity-50 with pointer events off. When a card, bar, or modal ends in two buttons, the primary goes on the right and fills the width, the secondary sits left at its own width.

heading: Icons
text: Font Awesome Pro, classic solid by default, classic regular for a few outlines like the clipboard and the star. An icon is . Size and color come from Tailwind text utilities, never fa-lg or fa-2x. Brands is for a third-party logo, like . Light, thin, duotone, and sharp stay unused so icons keep one weight.

heading: Review checklist
text: Page is slate-200 with white or glass cards. Nothing white sits directly on white. Body text is slate-700, headings slate-800 extrabold, links sky-700. Every neutral control is one rung from its background, and its label carries the contrast. Each accent appears at 300 (control) or the 100 tint (label), never elsewhere. One sky primary action per screen. Good is sky, not green. Default text is text-sm. No all caps. Corners are rounded-2xl on cards, rounded-xl on default buttons. Icons are fa-solid or fa-regular only, sized with text utilities.
Two layout sections make a page. The navbar runs the full width of the window. The main content area has its width capped. Source of truth: /docs/patterns/page-structure and /docs/components/navbar.

heading: The shell
text: Message Hub and the workflow builder drop the max width, because that work needs the whole window. Everything else keeps it. The navbar is the one dark surface (slate-700). Neutral controls inside it are slate-600, hover slate-500, with white text. Accent buttons keep their 300 fill.

heading: Headings and spacing
text: The page title sits directly on the page background, text-2xl xl:text-3xl font-extrabold text-slate-800. Every other heading sits inside a card with its content. The gap between cards is gap-4 md:gap-6 xl:gap-8 on every layout, and it never exceeds the padding between the container and the window edge. The grid lives on the main content, not on body, so padding and gaps stay separate from the navbar.

heading: Base layout
text: Dashboards, item lists, analytics. A left-aligned 12-column grid filled with cards.

heading: Create pages
text: Creating a campaign, a segment, a contact. A centered single column, and these are the only pages that center. A flex column with cards centered, each card w-full md:max-w-2xl. The page description sits on the page background directly under the heading. The cards are usually glass, since they hold inputs.

heading: Sidebar pages
text: Edit screens, analytics, settings. Sidebar and content in a flex row from md up, stacked below that. Small cards in the content column are w-full md:max-w-2xl, aligned left, the same width as create-page cards. Content that needs room (tables, overviews) uses w-full. A settings page mixes both in one column.

heading: Review checklist
text: Navbar full width, main content capped with the container classes above. Page title on the background, all other headings inside cards. One consistent gap between cards, matching the container padding. Create flows are the only centered pages. Form and settings cards cap at max-w-2xl. Tables and overviews run full width.
Real Voxie screens stripped of every class, for testing guidance and rules.
